declared_proposition: For every prime q>5 define the exact integers U=(2^(q-1)-1)/q and V=(3^(q-1)-1)/q, and define P_q=5U-3V+q(10U^2-3V^2)+q^2(10U^3-V^3)+5q^3U^4+q^4U^5. Then exactly 32^(q-1)-27^(q-1)=qP_q and 2^(q-1)-3^(q-1)=q(U-V). Consequently, for every integer r>=1, q^(r+1) divides the first difference if and only if P_q=0 modulo q^r, and divides the second difference if and only if U-V=0 modulo q^r. Equivalently their exact q-adic valuations are 1+v_q(P_q) and 1+v_q(U-V), respectively.
mathematical_argument: The definitions give 2^(q-1)=1+qU and 3^(q-1)=1+qV as exact integer equalities. Since 32^(q-1)=(1+qU)^5 and 27^(q-1)=(1+qV)^3, expanding both binomials and subtracting gives the displayed five-term P_q identity with no omitted tail. Direct subtraction gives the U-V identity. Both differences are nonzero, so taking q-adic valuations and reducing modulo arbitrary q^r are valid.

reproducible_computation.no_go_scope: The identities decide every q-adic depth once U,V are supplied, but they do not compare v_q(P_q) with v_q(U-V) uniformly over all primes. The finite replay is not an all-prime valuation theorem and these two fixed bases still encode only one local run-block route, not arbitrary Collatz trajectories or nontrivial cycles.

finite_computation_boundary: Five q-adic quotient digits are replayed for all 17,981 primes through 200,000; exact identities hold for arbitrary depth, but the finite valuation histogram proves no all-prime inequality.
logical_limit: The all-depth identity removes the omitted-digit gap but supplies no uniform valuation domination over all primes and no global Collatz trajectory argument.

route_decision.retain: an all-prime comparison between v_q(P_q) and v_q(U_q-V_q), now with every higher digit represented by one exact finite polynomial

claim_boundary: No Collatz proof, divergent orbit, or nontrivial cycle; an exact all-depth fixed-base valuation identity and bounded five-digit replay only.
